pageDescription: AI-generated and AI-assisted research notes in quantum information science
introduction: AI4Science collects exploratory research notes developed through sustained interaction with generative AI. Each entry presents the scientific question and the scope of the result. These notes are working documents rather than peer-reviewed publications.

Most of the prose and derivations in these notes are generated by ChatGPT through an interactive research process. I guide the work by setting the research direction, formulating questions, checking and challenging intermediate claims, and contributing new ideas.

notes.label: AI-generated note
notes.title: Exact PVM-Incompatibility-Breaking Criterion for a Broad Class of Nonunital Qubit Channels
paragraphs: This note studies when a nonunital qubit channel destroys the incompatibility of every finite family of qubit projective measurements (PVMs), so that all output PVMs become jointly measurable.

For unital qubit channels, exact analytical criteria are known. Before this note, analytical results for nonunital channels were available only in special cases, while broader cases could be investigated numerically through the compatible-radius framework introduced by Nguyen, Nguyen, and Gühne in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 240401 (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09349).

Every qubit channel acts affinely on Bloch vectors. Writing this action as **r → D r + t**, the channel is characterized by a real 3 × 3 matrix **D** and a translation vector **t**. The translation breaks the central symmetry that makes the unital problem more tractable.

The note does not solve the full nonunital problem. It derives an exact PVM-incompatibility-breaking criterion for the large family of channels satisfying **||D⁻¹t|| ≤ 1** when **D** is invertible - equivalently, channels whose output ellipsoid contains the origin. This region is referred to as the **inner branch**. The result also extends continuously to singular Bloch matrices through an inverse-free formulation, while the outer branch remains open.

This note builds on my research on POVM incompatibility and quantum steering. In my paper with Eric Chitambar, [Exact Steering Bound for Two-Qubit Werner States — Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 250201 (2024)](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.250201), we showed that PVMs and arbitrary POVMs have the same steering threshold for two-qubit Werner states. My recent preprint, [Exact Incompatibility-Breaking Criterion for Unital Qubit Channels — arXiv:2607.27757](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27757), extends this equivalence to every unital qubit channel: PVMs already determine the incompatibility-breaking boundary for arbitrary POVMs.

The present note is intended as a first step toward an exact incompatibility-breaking criterion for arbitrary POVMs under general nonunital qubit channels. A central open question is whether the POVM and PVM boundaries also coincide in the nonunital setting; this conjecture has been explored extensively through numerical tests.
